The present claim petition has been filed by the petitioners against the respondents under Section 166 of SCCH-10 Motor Vehicles Act seeking compensation of Rs.1,00,00,000/- with interest for the death of Smt. Kanyakumari in a Road Traffic Accident that occurred on 08.02.2024.
2.

The case of the petitioners in brief is as under:
That, on 08.02.2024 at about 7.00 a.m., when the deceased was proceeding on the Scooter bearing Reg. No.KA- 43-W-4814 as a pillion rider and the same was ridden by one A. Venkatesh from Malleshwaram to Vasanthnagar and when they reached near Chakravarthy Layout, Palace road, Bengaluru, at that time, the respondent No.2/ rider of the Scooter bearing Reg. No.KA-04-JJ-8334 came from same direction with high speed in a rash and negligent manner and dashed to the deceased scooter from behind, as a result, she fell down and sustained grievous injuries.

Immediately,
she was shifted to Bhagwan Mahaveer Jain hospital, Bengaluru and during the course of treatment she underwent surgery.
She succumbed to the fatal injuries on 19.03.2024.
They spent Rs.50,00,000/- towards treatment SCCH-10 and medicines and Rs.30,000/- towards transportation of dead body and funeral obsequies.
The petitioner No.1 is husband and petitioner No.2 and 3 are children of the deceased.

Prior to the accident, the deceased was hale and healthy, aged about 59 years and she Venkatesh A vs Reshma Parveen on 3 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/58759040/
2 was doing Tailoring work on her own and earning Rs.30,000/- per month.
Due to the death of deceased, the petitioners have put to mental shock and agony and also lost their bread earner of the family.

Further, the accident was occurred due to the rash and negligent riding of the respondent No.2 /
rider of the offending Scooter.
As such, the respondent No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioners.
Hence, this claim petition.
3. After presentation of the petition, notice was issued to the respondent No.1 and 2 (owner and rider of the motor cycle).
Despite of service of notice, respondents have not appeared before the Court, remained absent and were placed exparte.
SCCH-10 4.
In order to prove the case, the petitioner No.1 examined himself as PW-1 and got marked documents as Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.18.

Bengaluru, at that time, the rider of the Scooter bearing Reg. No.KA-04-JJ-8334 came from same direction with high speed and in a rash and negligent manner and dashed to the deceased scooter, as a result, she fell down and sustained fatal injuries and died while taking treatment at the hospital?

?

If yes, for what quantum ?

4) What order or award?

sentences.text: The petitioner has filed this petition claiming compensation of Rs.1,00,00,000/- on account of death of Smt. Kanyakumari in the road traffic accident.
9. The petitioner No.1 stepped into the witness box and SCCH-10 examined himself as PW-1.
On behalf of the petitioners, 18 documents were marked as per Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.18.
Ex.P.1 is the copy of the FIR No.0025/2024 of High Grounds Traffic Police and Ex.P.2 is the First information statement.
On perusal of Ex.P.1 and Ex.P.2, it reveal that I.O. has registered a case against the rider of the offending Scooter bearing Reg. No.KA-04-JJ-8334.
Ex.P.6 is the seizure mahazar wherein it reveals that during investigation I.O. has seized the offending vehicle.
Ex.P.13 is the charge sheet filed by the High Grounds Traffic police against one Mr. Mustaqh Ahmed who is none other than the rider of the offending vehicle.
On perusal of the aforesaid documents, it is sufficient to conclude that, the accident in question had taken place due to the actionable negligence of the rider of the offending vehicle.
10. Besides, it is settled principles of law that in a motor vehicles accident compensation cases strict proof of negligence is not required.

This view receives support from SCCH-10 the law declared by Hon'ble Apex Court in a decision reported in 2009(13) SCC page 530 in the case of Bimla Devi and others Vs. Himachalapradesh Road Transport Corporation and in AIR 2011 SC page 1504 in the case of Parameshwari Vs. Amir Chand and others.

Thus, by considering the present facts of the case and the materials placed on record, I am of the opinion that, the accident in question had occurred due to the rash and negligent riding of the rider of the Scooter bearing Reg. No.KA-04-JJ-8334 and deceased Kanyakumari died due to the accident.
Hence, Point No.1 is answered in the Affirmative.
11. POINT No.2:-

It is the contention of the petitioners that, the petitioner No.1 is the husband and petitioner No.2 and 3 are the son and married daughter of the deceased and they were SCCH-10 wholly depending upon the service of the deceased at home and also on her earnings.
In order to prove the relationship with the deceased, the petitioners have produced the copies of Aadhaar cards and Election ID card as per Ex.P.14 to Ex.P.16.

In the instant case, the respondents have not appeared before the Court and not contested the petition and there is no dispute regarding the relationship of the Venkatesh A vs Reshma Parveen on 3 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/58759040/
4 petitioners with the deceased.
Therefore, this Court is of the opinion that, the petitioners are the legal heirs of the deceased.
Accordingly I answer Point No.2 in the Affirmative.
12. POINT No.3:
It is the specific contention of the petitioner that, deceased Kanyakumari was hale and healthy at the time of accident and was doing Tailoring work and earning Rs.30,000/- per month.
It is further contended that, due to untimely death of deceased they were put to great hardship.
SCCH-10 13.
To prove the age of the deceased, the petitioners have not produced any documents.
On perusal of Inquest and PM report i.e. Ex.P.8 and Ex.P.9, wherein the age of the deceased is shown as 59 years.
Since there is no corroborative documents regarding the age of the deceased, this Tribunal considers the age of the deceased as 59 years on the date of accident.
14. Further, to prove the occupation and income of the deceased, the petitioners have not produced any document.
At this juncture, I would like to refer the decision reported in 2023(4) KCCR 3603 (DB) between Aneesahemmed Vs Mohammed Yusuf and Another.

sentences.text: In the above decision the Hon'ble High Court has taken into consideration the notional income as fixed by the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority, Bengaluru (KSLSA in short).

sentences.text: The KSLSA, Bengaluru as per letter dated 26.02.2022 - 01/NLA/2022/550/2022 has circulated the notional income chart prepared by them.
As per the said notional income SCCH-10 chart, if the accident occurred in the year 2022, the notional income has to be taken as Rs.15,500/- per month.

Therefore, in view of the decision of the Hon'ble High Court and the letter of KSLSA and also in the absence of proof of income, this Court is of the opinion that, if the notional income is taken into consideration for assessing the income of the deceased would be just and proper.
The accident was occurred on 08-02-2024.
Therefore, this Court has taken Rs.16,500/- as monthly income of the deceased.

The Hon'ble Apex Court in the judgment reported in 2020 ACJ 759 in the case of National Insurance Co. Ltd., Vs Birender & Others

sentences.text: , held that it must necessarily follow that, even the major, married and earning sons of the deceased being the legal representatives have a right to apply for compensation and it would be bounden duty of the Tribunal to consider the application irrespective of the fact whether the concerned legal representative was fully dependent on the deceased and not to limit the claim towards conventional SCCH-10 heads only.
18. In Sarla Verma case, the Hon'ble Apex Court has expressed the view regarding standardized deduction towards personal and living expenses.
where the number of dependents are 2 to 3, the deduction would be 1/3rd.
As discussed supra, in the present case, petitioners are the husband, son and daughter and they are the dependents.
Hence, in the present case, 1/3rd of the income of the deceased has to be deducted towards personal and living expenses.
In the present case, the Court has taken the view that the deceased was having monthly income of Rs.16,500/- (by relying on KSLSA notional income chart) and annual income would be Rs.1,98,000/-.

If 1/3 rd is deducted towards personal expenses, the contribution to the family (dependents) is determined as Rs.1,32,000/-.
19.
In the present case, the deceased was aged 59 years at the time of accident and she was self employed.
Hence, an addition 10% is warranted towards future prospects.

If 10% is added to the personal income of the deceased, it would be Rs.1,45,200/-.
The multiplier will be 9 having regard to the age of the deceased at the time of death (59 years).
Therefore, the total loss of dependency would be Rs.1,45,200/- X 9 = Rs.13,06,800/-.

consortium and funeral expenses.

23. The petitioners have contended that immediately after the accident the injured was shifted to Bhagwan Mahaveer Jain hospital, Bengaluru and admitted as an inpatient on 08.02.2024 and under went surgery and succumbed to the injuries in the hospital on 19.03.2024.
It is further stated that, the petitioners have spent Rs.50,00,000/- towards medical expenses.
The petitioners have produced the medical bills amounting to Rs.11,74,881/- as per Ex.P.17 and medical prescriptions as per Ex.P.18.
Sl.No.1 and Sl.No.2 in Ex.P.17 are the SCCH-10 final medical bills amounting to Rs.9,00,752/- and Rs.51,309/- respectively.
Sl. No.3 to Sl.No.82 are the tax invoices, OPD cash memos and bills in respect of dialysis.
Therefore, Sl.No.3 to Sl.No.82 medical bills are not taken into consideration.
The final bills i.e. Sl.No.1 and Sl.No.2 in Ex.P.17 appears to be genuine.
Hence, the petitioners are entitled for medical bills of Rs.9,00,752/- + Rs.51,309/- = Rs.9,52,061/- and same is rounded off to Rs.9,52,000/- under the head of medical expenses.

25 . As far as liability is concerned, in the instant case, the respondent No.1 is the owner and respondent No.2 is the rider of the offending vehicle.
Further, as per the police records, the offending vehicle was not insured at the time of accident.

Therefore, the respondent No.1 and 2 being owner and rider of the offending vehicle bearing Reg. No.KA-04-JJ- 8334 are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation of Rs.24,38,800/- with interest @ 6% p.a. to the petitioners from the date of petition till its realization in the ratio of 40:30:30 respectively.
Accordingly, I answer the Point No.3 Partly in the Affirmative.
26. Point No.4:

In view of my finding on Point No.1 to 3, I proceed to pass the following:
SCCH-10 ORDER under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 is partly allowed with costs.

The petitioners are entitled for total compensation of Rs.24,38,800/-(Rupees Twenty Four Lakhs Thirty Eight Thousand Eight Hundred only) with simple interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of petition till realization of entire compensation awarded.
Petitioners are entitled to receive compensation in the ratio of 40:30:30 respectively.
The respondent No.1 and 2 are directed to deposit the entire compensation amount with interest within 30 days from the date of this order.

Out of the award amount, 50% of the award amount of petitioners shall be invested in fixed deposit for a period of 3 years in any nationalized bank and balance amount shall be released in favour SCCH-10 of the petitioners through NEFT/RTGS by way of E- payment on proper identification.

Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-
Draw award accordingly.
